subject: Performance validation kickoff — throughput & streaming plan

Date: Wed, 4 Jul 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance deep-dive follow-up / targets

Sofia / team — thanks again for the demo this morning. Anna and I sketched target SLOs after the call and wanted to confirm so you can size a pilot: 

- Streaming latency: 95th percentile end-to-end token latency <= 120ms (we measure client->response).
- Concurrency: sustained concurrent sessions ~250; burst spikes to 600 for short windows.
- Throughput: peak sustained QPS ~1,500; token throughput during peak bursts ~6,000 tokens/sec aggregated.
- Session lengths: median streaming session ~1.2k tokens, top 10% up to 12k tokens.
- Availability: target 99.9% during business hours, fallback to lower-cost model acceptable for <5% of requests during capacity events.

Two asks for the pilot kickoff:
1) Can Redwood propose a pilot plan that validates latency at 95p under realistic streaming shapes?
2) We need a cost/throughput comparison of A100-40GB vs H100-80GB for our workload — we'd like tradeoffs (cost per 1k requests, expected headroom).

I attached a short doc with our traffic sample and the SOC2 checklist that procurement will gate on (novacorp_perf_requirements.pdf).

Kevin

Thanks Kevin — great summary. Putting a quick post-call plan together and next steps below. Attaching a draft pilot plan (draft-pilot-plan.xlsx) that maps the scenarios you outlined to measurable benchmarks.

Recap of what we heard (confirm if any of this is off):
- 95p streaming latency <= 120ms (client->token).
- Sustained concurrency ~250, bursts to 600; peak token throughput ~6k tok/s.
- Sessions up to 12k tokens (important for KV cache sizing).
- Availability target 99.9% BH, with graceful degradation policy for non-critical calls.

Proposed pilot (2 weeks):
- Environment: Dedicated pool (isolated) in us-west region.
- Compare two hardware profiles: H100-80GB (priority low-latency path) vs A100-40GB (cost-optimized).
- Reserved throughput lanes: baseline reservation for 1,500 QPS equivalent and a burst/overflow policy.
- Benchmarks: steady-state QPS, streaming 95p latency, long-session KV-cache warm/cold, failover to fallback model.
- Success criteria: measured 95p latency <=120ms under simulated traffic, <5% error spike during burst, and cost-per-1k-requests targets (we'll estimate after initial numbers).

Subject: RE: Performance deep-dive follow-up / targets — bench notes

Sofia — quick technical notes to seed the pilot plan. High level recommendations below.

Hardware tradeoffs (short):
- H100-80GB: stronger for very low-latency streaming due to faster FP16 kernels and larger HBM for long KV caches. Expect ~15-25% lower 95p latency on identical batching configurations vs A100 for models with large context and active streaming.
- A100-40GB: better cost efficiency for batchy workloads; may need quantized variants and aggressive batch tuning to hit the same throughput. For long-session KV-heavy traffic, memory pressure may cause eviction-induced latency spikes unless we pin fewer concurrent sessions per GPU.

Sizing heuristics we will test in pilot (bench matrix):
1) Streaming 95p sweep: concurrency buckets [100, 250, 400, 600], simulated session lengths [1.2k, 6k, 12k tokens]. Measure 95p end-to-end.
2) Throughput baseline: sustained QPS 500, 1.5k, 3k — measure tokens/sec and token cost.
3) Cold-warm cache transition: start with empty KV caches and run 10k warmup sessions; observe tail latency.
4) Fallback scenarios: saturate primary pool and route to lower-cost variant; verify graceful degradation and correctness.

Reserved throughput: propose initial reservation equivalent to 1,500 QPS using a pool with headroom for 2x burst. We'll provide a recommended pool size per hardware type in the bench summary.

Operational notes: prewarm KV caches for expected session topologies; enable continuous batching with short batching windows (6–8ms) for streaming; instrument per-token tracing on a 1% sample.

Deliverables timeline:
- Thu EOD: bench matrix + cost estimate (Sofia/Karthik).
- Next Tue: pilot kickoff and runbook (Ben to coordinate MAP + PO).
